title: Sobriety for entering the tabernacle
english: They are not to drink wine or strong drink when they enter the tabernacle (Leviticus 10:9). The drunkenness of the world hinders vision. Be sober (1 Peter 5:8).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is applying the priestly rule about not drinking wine or strong drink when entering the tabernacle to the soul's need for sobriety in order to see spiritual things.

title: The Drunkenness of the Saints
english: There is a drunkenness of the saints—by the Spirit, not by wine. The apostles were thought to be full of new wine (Acts 2:13). Distinguish the cups.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining that the priests' prohibition of wine points to a spiritual sobriety, and he now contrasts worldly drunkenness with the holy intoxication of the Spirit.

title: The priest's teaching office: discernment, not surface judgment
english: That they may distinguish between the holy and the profane, the clean and the unclean (Leviticus 10:10). This is the office of teaching. Do not judge the surface.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the priestly duty to distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean, and he warns against judging by appearances.

title: Clean animal: split hoof and chewing cud
english: A clean animal is one that has a split hoof and chews the cud. Chewing the cud is meditation on the law; the split hoof is discernment of works. You must have both.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the Levitical distinction between clean and unclean animals as a figure for the soul's need for both meditation on the law and discernment in works.

title: Camel, pig, and the insufficiency of one mark alone
english: The camel chews the cud but does not split the hoof; the pig splits the hoof but does not chew the cud. Both are unclean. One without the other is not enough. Faith with works.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the clean-animal rule from Leviticus, applying the two marks (chewing the cud and the split hoof) to the soul's need for both meditation and discernment.

title: Clean fish: scales and fins as virtues and upward motion
english: In the waters, those creatures that have fins and scales are clean. The scales are the virtues; the fins are movement toward the higher things. Without these, one is sunk down.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the clean animals of Leviticus, now applying the fish that have fins and scales to the soul's virtues and movement toward higher things.

title: Holiness as separation from uncleanness
english: "Be holy, because I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2). Separation from the uncleanness of the soul. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is concluding his moral application of the clean and unclean creatures, quoting Leviticus' command to be holy and applying it to the soul.
